title: Streamline CI image layering and cache warmup to cut build times
creator: Ava Patel
description: Current GitHub Actions workflows suffer from long cold-cache times and redundant layer invalidation across many repositories. This ticket focuses on three complementary improvements: 1) refactor Dockerfile layering across core infra images to maximize cache reuse; 2) implement an automated cache-warmup job that populates remote buildkit cache for the most-used base images before scheduled CI runs; 3) upgrade and standardize toolchain binaries (golangci-lint, node toolchains, Rust/cargo cache strategy) inside curated CI images so per-repo setup time is minimized. Goal: reduce median CI wall-clock time for unit/integration builds by 35% and reduce build-worker churn from repeated full-image rebuilds.
acceptance_criteria: Median unit/integration workflow time across core services reduced by >= 35% in the 14-day A/B window compared to baseline (dashboard: CI Build Time v2)
Remote buildkit cache hits for infra-base images >= 80% during working hours for two consecutive weeks
All repo Dockerfiles using the new layering guidelines or inheriting from curated infra images
Toolchain versions (golangci-lint, node, cargo/sccache) pinned and preinstalled in infra images; individual repos no longer download these during every run
Documented rollback plan and smoke tests for cache-warmup job; one on-call runbook update referencing this ticket
work_items: Audit top-40 repos by CI runtime to identify Dockerfile patterns that cause frequent layer invalidation
Create new infra-base-image v11 with reorganized layers: system deps -> language runtimes -> build tools -> thin app layer
Add buildx cache-to=registry and cache-from logic to publish layer cache artifacts to our registry-backed blob store
Implement nightly cache-warmup GH Action that pulls & builds most-common targets to populate buildkit cache
Replace per-repo ad-hoc tool installer steps with base image preinstalled binaries and environment variables
Add actions/cache for pip wheels/npm cache where appropriate with standardized cache keys
Benchmarks: run before/after matrix on sample repos and feed results to CI Build Time v2 dashboard
Rollout plan: opt-in label on repos; automated PR generation for Dockerfile updates; monitor for two weeks before org-wide enforcement
decisions: Adopt BuildKit's cache-to=registry strategy (vs. uploading full images to Docker Hub) to reduce registry egress costs and simplify cache invalidation windows
Use sccache + remote cache for Rust-heavy repos rather than cargo locals to get cross-run benefit
Pin golangci-lint to 1.59.0 (after compatibility checks) and include in infra-base-image instead of dynamic install
Node versions will be standardized to 20.x LTS for server-side tools; frontend teams can opt out by explicit justification
Nightly cache-warmup limited to off-peak hours (04:00-06:00 UTC) to avoid rate limiting and CI interference
blockers: Need registry credentials & permissions for cache-to writes from GitHub Actions (pending infra ticket INF-3261)
Legal review for caching third-party binaries in internal registry (waiting response from Legal, expected 2026-03-12)
Some mono-repos have custom build steps that may break when base image changes — require maintainers to opt into staging tests
